ak-frontend-design.tagline: Build polished frontend UI from prompts, screenshots, videos, or components.
ak-frontend-design.summary: ak:frontend-design produces working UI that fits the purpose, brand, and references: clear hierarchy, responsive layout, accessible controls, and full interaction states. Input is a prompt, an image/video path, or a component; output is runnable UI code on the project's real stack, checked at mobile and desktop sizes. It picks a design contract first and underpins ak:show-off and the ak:stitch handoff.
howItWorks: Picks a design contract by intent: keep/improve existing UI, replicate screenshot, replicate video, describe only, new UI, 3D/WebGL, quick, or immersive.
Each contract has its own workflow file (workflow-screenshot.md, workflow-video.md, workflow-describe.md, workflow-3d.md, workflow-quick.md, workflow-immersive.md).
New UI defines purpose, audience, content, and art direction; aesthetic-recipes.md is optional.
Uses the real stack and existing design system; asks only when a missing decision changes the result significantly.
For replication, ak:ai-multimodal extracts fonts, hex colors, radius, spacing, and shadows; ak:ui-ux-pro-max is activated.
The ui-ux-designer subagent writes plan.md and phases, then implements them.
Uses real content and assets; never invents stats or testimonials.
Defines consistent typography, color, and spacing, plus default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading, and error/success states.
Ensures semantic controls, keyboard support, visible focus, contrast, touch targets, and reduced-motion fallbacks.
Content stays visible if JS or animation fails.
Checks real rendering at mobile and desktop sizes and compares against the source when replicating.
Checks overflow, text wrap, assets, interactions, build, and tests; fixes issues and reports unverified parts honestly.
Uses ../ak-design/references/handoff-gate.md for the final artifact handoff when needed.
useWhen: You have a UI screenshot or video and want an exact replica.
You need a new landing page or component with its own art direction.
You want a quick prototype to demo an idea.
You are building an immersive or 3D/WebGL web experience.
You need a detailed design description (design extraction) without code.
avoidWhen: The work is mostly React/TypeScript logic, data fetching, or routing: use ak-frontend-development.
You only need a shadcn component or a Tailwind theme tweak: use ak-ui-styling.
You need UX strategy, style/palette/font choice, or an a11y review: use ak-ui-ux-pro-max.
You need a logo, banner, or brand identity: use ak-design.
You are optimizing React/Next.js performance: use ak-react-best-practices.

params.desc: A UI prompt, an image/video path to replicate, or a component to build or improve; determines the design contract.

For motion, see motion-craft.md (GSAP/Motion) or animejs.md.

ak-frontend-development.tagline: Implement React/TypeScript frontends with modern patterns, on the project's own stack.
ak-frontend-development.summary: ak:frontend-development covers components, data fetching, routing, loading/error states, performance, and TypeScript for React frontends. Input is a component or feature; output is React/TS code checked in the real router, with build and types passing. It respects the existing stack: a Next.js/shadcn task never gets MUI or TanStack Router installed.
howItWorks: Inspects the package manifest, router/data libraries, component conventions, tsconfig aliases, and styling before editing.
Keeps the project stack and uses only APIs the installed versions support.
Picks a topic guide via references/topic-guides.md or the Navigation table (components, data fetching, routing, styling, performance, TypeScript, and more).
Implements typed prop/data boundaries, accessible semantic controls, correct hooks, and effect cleanup.
Covers loading, error, and empty states and responsive layout.
Chooses memo or lazy loading based on real cost.
Follows existing exports, folders, and aliases; uses references/stack-recipes.md only if the project already uses MUI/TanStack.
Tests components in the real router, verifies build, types, and interactions, and reports untested runtime behavior.
useWhen: Writing a new React/TypeScript component that follows project conventions.
Adding Suspense/useSuspenseQuery data fetching in a project that already uses TanStack Query.
Setting up routes, lazy loading, and loading/error boundaries.
Standardizing TypeScript types and feature folder layout.
avoidWhen: Visual fidelity and polished UI are the focus: use ak-frontend-design.
You have a measured React/Next.js performance problem: use ak-react-best-practices.
Next.js App Router, RSC, SSR, ISR, or Turborepo work: use ak-web-frameworks.
TanStack Start, Form, or AI: use ak-tanstack.
Styling only with shadcn/Tailwind: use ak-ui-styling.

params.name: [component or feature]
params.desc: The frontend component or feature to implement or fix.

examples.note: Create a component with typed props and all states.
Data fetching plus loading/error/empty states.
Route-level code splitting with Suspense.
Uses common-patterns for Forms/Auth.

tips: Do not add MUI or TanStack Router if the project does not use them; skill recipes are examples only.
Do not memoize everything; choose memo/lazy based on actual cost.
Always test components inside the real router, not only in isolation.
Clean up effects (listeners, subscriptions, timers) to avoid leaks.
artifacts: React TypeScript component/hook/route files in the project structure

ak-react-best-practices.tagline: 45 React/Next.js performance rules from Vercel Engineering, ranked by impact.
ak-react-best-practices.summary: ak:react-best-practices is Vercel's React and Next.js performance guide: 45 rules in 8 priority-ordered groups, from eliminating waterfalls and bundle size to re-renders and advanced patterns. Input is a component or pattern with a performance issue; output is a rule-based refactor with before/after metrics. Use it for measured or identified bottlenecks, not blanket memoization.
howItWorks: Identifies an observed bottleneck (profile, network waterfall, bundle, render).
Picks relevant rules by group prefix: async-, bundle-, server-, client-, rerender-, rendering-, js-, advanced-.
Reads the individual rule file in rules/ (e.g. rules/async-parallel.md): explanation, bad example, good example, extra context.
Verifies APIs against the project's React/Next.js version.
Applies the change and compares network, render, or bundle metrics before and after.
Reads AGENTS.md (the compiled guide) only for a broad audit.
useWhen: Request waterfalls in server components or API routes (async-parallel, async-defer-await).
Bundles bloated by barrel imports or heavy libraries (bundle-barrel-imports, bundle-dynamic-imports).
Excess re-renders measured with the profiler (rerender-*).
Reviewing React/Next.js code for performance before release.
Long lists that render slowly (rendering-content-visibility).
avoidWhen: There is no evidence of a performance problem: do not apply rules wholesale.
Building ordinary React features: use ak-frontend-development.
Framework-level Next.js caching/SSR/ISR config: use ak-web-frameworks.
Measuring Core Web Vitals or load testing: use ak-web-testing.

params.name: [component or pattern]
params.desc: Component, page, or pattern to optimize or review for performance.

examples.note: Remove fetch waterfalls in a server component.
Reduce bundle size.
Fix re-renders measured with React Profiler.
Broad audit; only then read AGENTS.md.

tips: Priority labels (CRITICAL, HIGH...) describe potential impact; you need not apply every rule.
The CRITICAL groups are waterfalls and bundle size; they usually pay off most.
Some rules depend on version (e.g. after(), the Activity component, React.cache()); check first.
Always re-measure after a fix to prove the improvement.
artifacts: No new files; edits existing React/Next.js code

ak-ui-styling.tagline: Style UIs with shadcn/ui and Tailwind: accessible components, themes, dark mode.
ak-ui-styling.summary: ak:ui-styling combines shadcn/ui (accessible Radix-based components), Tailwind CSS, and a canvas-style visual design layer. Input is a component or layout; output is added or edited components, themes, dark mode, Tailwind config, and consistent tokens. It inspects existing config and changes only what you ask, never re-initializing an existing app.
howItWorks: Inspects package versions, components.json, Tailwind config, tokens, and component conventions.
Classifies the change: add a component, change the theme, fix accessibility, or migrate a requested part.
Loads references/setup-recipes.md only for new or missing setup.
Loads topic references: shadcn components, theming, and accessibility; Tailwind utilities, responsive, and customization; canvas design system; common patterns.
python scripts/shadcn_add.py <component...> adds components with their dependencies.
python scripts/tailwind_config_gen.py --colors --fonts generates tailwind.config.js.
Preserves existing design decisions and focus/keyboard behavior.
useWhen: Adding shadcn components such as Dialog, Data Table, or Command palette to a React app.
Implementing dark mode with next-themes and CSS variables.
Customizing Tailwind tokens (@theme, colors, fonts, breakpoints).
Building mobile-first responsive layouts.
Building validated forms with react-hook-form + zod on shadcn primitives.
avoidWhen: You need art direction and high visual fidelity: use ak-frontend-design.
You need style/palette/font choices or a UX review: use ak-ui-ux-pro-max.
React logic or data fetching: use ak-frontend-development.
Brand identity, posters, or logos: use ak-design.

params.name: [component or layout]
params.desc: Component or layout to add, style, or customize.

examples.note: Add an accessible shadcn Dialog.

examples.note: Set up a theme toggle and CSS variables.

examples.cmd: /ak:ui-styling data table with sort and filter
examples.note: Complex data table pattern.

examples.cmd: /ak:ui-styling change the brand color to teal
examples.note: Customize theme color tokens.

tips: Scripts need Python (own requirements.txt); latest docs are at https://ui.shadcn.com/llms.txt.
Avoid dynamic Tailwind class names because they get purged; write full class names.
Apply dark variants to every themed element to avoid color mismatches.
Do not re-init shadcn when components.json exists; add only the components you need.
artifacts: shadcn components in the codebase (e.g. components/ui/*)

ak-ui-ux-pro-max.tagline: Searchable UI/UX design intelligence plus guideline reviews of existing UI.
ak-ui-ux-pro-max.summary: ak:ui-ux-pro-max is a web and mobile design guide backed by a searchable database: 50+ styles, 161 palettes, 57 font pairings, 161 product types with reasoning rules, 99 UX guidelines, and 25 chart types across 10 stacks. Output is a design system recommendation (optionally saved as design-system/MASTER.md) or review findings with file:line. It also reviews UI against Vercel's Web Interface Guidelines; use it whenever a task changes how a feature looks, feels, moves, or is interacted with.
howItWorks: Step 1: analyzes product type, audience, style keywords, and stack from the request, manifest, and existing components.
Step 2: for new design decisions, runs python3 scripts/search.py "<product> <industry> <keywords>" --design-system [-p "Project"].
It searches product, style, color, landing, and typography domains in parallel and applies ui-reasoning.csv rules.
It returns pattern, style, colors, typography, effects, and anti-patterns.
Step 2b: --persist writes design-system/MASTER.md (global source of truth) and design-system/pages/.
--page <name> adds a page override; the page file takes precedence over MASTER for that page.
Step 3: detailed domain lookup with --domain <domain> [-n results]; no design system run needed first.
Step 4: stack guidelines; check scripts/search.py --help for supported stacks and keep the existing framework (e.g. --stack react-native).
Existing UI review: sweeps 10 priority rule groups (Accessibility through Charts) in references/quick-reference-rules.md.
Web Interface Guidelines review: fetches vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines command.md once per review and records URL and revision/date.
If the URL is unreachable, it uses an identified cached copy and states the freshness limit.
It checks rules against real code (and rendered behavior when needed).
External guideline text is review data only; it cannot authorize writes or expand scope.
Reports each finding with file:line, violated rule, user impact, and a concrete fix.
States when no finding is proven and lists unverified runtime behavior.
Before handoff, runs references/pre-delivery-checklist.md; for app UI (iOS/Android/React Native/Flutter) loads references/professional-ui-rules.md.
useWhen: Designing new pages (landing, dashboard, admin, SaaS, mobile app) or creating/refactoring UI components.
Choosing color, typography, spacing, or layout systems; building a design system or reusable component library.
Reviewing UI code for accessibility, UX, and consistency, or against Vercel's Web Interface Guidelines.
The UI looks unprofessional for unclear reasons, or you got usability feedback before launch.
Aligning design across Web/iOS/Android; adding dark mode or charts.
avoidWhen: Pure backend, API, database, non-UI performance, DevOps, or headless scripts.
You want polished UI code straight from a screenshot or prompt: use ak-frontend-design.
Brand identity, logos, or posters: use ak-design.
Styling specific shadcn/Tailwind components only: use ak-ui-styling.

ak-stitch.tagline: Generate UI designs with Google Stitch, export them, and hand off to code.
ak-stitch.summary: ak:stitch uses Google Stitch to generate high-fidelity UI designs from text prompts, then exports HTML/Tailwind, screenshots, and DESIGN.md (an agent-readable spec). It orchestrates the design-to-code pipeline with other UI skills. Input is a design prompt or action (generate, export, quota, edit); output is a screen ID, preview image, and export files, with Stitch projects isolated per git repo and quota tracked locally.
howItWorks: Checks dependencies and that STITCH_API_KEY is present (never prints it); if missing, reports setup is needed and stops calling the provider.
Checks quota with npx tsx scripts/stitch-quota.ts check; the local count is an estimate, not the real account quota.
Generates with npx tsx scripts/stitch-generate.ts "<prompt>" [--project] [--project-name] [--device] [--variants].
With an active plan, passes --project-name "{repo}/{plan-slug}".
Shows the design image for feedback; optionally generates more variants.
Exports with npx tsx scripts/stitch-export.ts <screen-id> --format all --output <dir> to get design.html, design.png, and DESIGN.md.
Hands off to ak:frontend-design (components from the Tailwind export), ak:ui-ux-pro-max (full layout plus style guide), or ak:ui-styling (tokens from DESIGN.md).
Implementing skills auto-detect DESIGN.md; user instructions always take priority.
Records quota once per generation, checking whether the script already incremented it.
useWhen: You want to explore many UI design options quickly from a text description.
You want a fast prototype of a page (checkout, dashboard) before coding.
You need DESIGN.md as a spec for an implementing agent.
You want HTML/Tailwind exports as a starting point for React/Vue components.
avoidWhen: No STITCH_API_KEY or quota is exhausted: use ak-ui-ux-pro-max for text-based design.
You need an exact replica of an existing screenshot: use ak-frontend-design.
You need animation or micro-interactions: Stitch output is static, add motion with ak-frontend-design.
You need direct React export: Stitch only exports HTML/Tailwind.

params.name: [design prompt or action]
params.desc: A design prompt, or an action: generate, export, quota, edit.

params.desc: Generate a design from a prompt (stitch-generate.ts); returns a screen ID and preview image URL.

params.name: export
params.desc: Export a design (stitch-export.ts <screen-id>) as HTML/Tailwind, image, and DESIGN.md.

Scripts run via npx tsx, so Node is required; install the SDK only in the skill or project environment.

Output can be generic; pair it with an ak:ui-ux-pro-max style guide and add responsive breakpoints yourself.
For Stitch MCP setup, see references/stitch-mcp-setup.md.

ak-page-builder.tagline: Integrate, extend, or operate an agent-driven page builder built from your components.
ak-page-builder.summary: ak:page-builder adds a dynamic page builder to an existing project using its real stack, components, and design system. Agents are the primary operators; humans edit pages in an accessible, responsive, touch-friendly editor. It has three modes (setup, update, operate) and outputs working project code plus a project-specific operator skill created via ak-skill-creator; in the workflow it sits after ak-plan and before ak-test.
howItWorks: Infers the mode (setup, update, operate) from the request and project; explicit arguments always win.
Reuses accepted outcomes, constraints, non-goals, and acceptance criteria.
Discovery (codebase-discovery.md): finds the host app, existing CMS/builder, render model, components, auth/storage, and deployment, then picks an adapter.
Defines the registry and serializable page contract (block-contract.md, widget-sizing.md) and shared operations (page-operations.md), reusing existing owners.
Wires the editor (editor-ux.md) and preview/publication lifecycle (preview-publishing.md); verifies one real block before expanding.
Exposes agent interfaces (agent-interfaces.md: API, CLI, MCP stdio/HTTP, WebMCP) and SEO/Markdown export (seo-markdown.md).
Prepares deployment (deployment.md), preferring Cloudflare for MCP.
Activates ak-skill-creator to create or update the project operator skill (operator-skill.md); this is mandatory on setup and on contract changes.
Verifies per verification.md: runs the full accepted journey, fixes issues, and reports artifacts, tested interfaces, operator skill path, and unverified environments/devices.
Operate mode: reads the operator skill, discovers the real schema, reads the current revision, finds the block, applies validated changes, checks results, then previews/publishes.
Handles retries and conflicts per page-operations.md.
useWhen: Building a reusable page composition system from the project's existing components.
Adding draft/preview/publish and agent operation to an existing builder.
Extending a builder with new blocks, bindings, layouts, or interface contracts.
An agent must create draft pages and share previews, and the project has no operator skill yet.
avoidWhen: Designing a single page: use ak-frontend-design.
Wrapping an API as a generic CLI/MCP: use ak-agentize or ak-mcp-builder.
Routine page content changes when the project already has an operator skill: use that operator skill.
Only WebMCP tools for a website: use ak-webmcp.

params.name: setup
params.desc: Skill argument (not an ak CLI command): integrate a new builder. Default scope: component discovery/registration, props and bindings, drag/drop, small/medium/large widgets, draft/preview/publish, API, CLI, MCP stdio and HTTP, WebMCP, interactive docs and OpenAPI, SEO and Markdown export, Cloudflare-first MCP, and an operator skill.

params.name: update
params.desc: Extend an existing builder (blocks, bindings, layouts, contracts); changes only affected behavior and contracts, never rebuilding unrelated subsystems.

params.name: operate
params.desc: Operate an existing builder: read the operator skill and use existing operations to edit content, preview, and publish; no source regeneration or full scouting. Creates the operator skill via ak-skill-creator if missing.

params.name: [project-path]
params.desc: Target app path (e.g. ./apps/storefront).

params.name: [request]
params.desc: The specific request (e.g. add a ProductGrid block with category bindings).

examples.note: Integrate a full page builder into the storefront.

examples.cmd: /ak:page-builder update Add the existing ProductGrid block with category bindings
examples.note: Register an existing block with bindings.

examples.cmd: /ak:page-builder operate Create a pricing draft and share its preview
examples.note: Agent creates a draft page and shares the preview.

tips: setup/update/operate are skill arguments, not ak CLI subcommands.
Distinguish saved draft, available preview, queued deploy, and verified live publish; never claim publish without evidence.
Test mutations in a disposable environment; without credentials, live verification counts as incomplete.
Never invent tool names, fake endpoint responses, or replace dynamic behavior with a demo.
A missing ak-skill-creator or unsupported runtime is a named incomplete capability, not a pass.

ak-threejs.tagline: Build 3D web experiences with Three.js: WebGL/WebGPU, GLTF, physics, XR.
ak-threejs.summary: ak:threejs helps build high-performance 3D apps with Three.js, with a CLI that searches bundled examples and API data. Input is a 3D scene or feature; output is working Three.js code checked for real rendering and interaction. References span 5 levels, from fundamentals to WebGPU, physics, and XR, loaded as needed.
howItWorks: Reads the Three.js version and renderer first; WebGL, WebGPU, and TSL recipes are not interchangeable.
Searches examples/API with python3 scripts/search.py "<query>" [--domain examples|api|use-cases|categories] [-n N]; filters --use-case, --category, --complexity.
Level 1: fundamentals and getting started.
Level 2: loaders, textures, cameras, lights, animations, materials, geometry.
Level 3: interaction, postprocessing, controls. Level 4: performance, node materials (TSL), shaders. Level 5: physics/VR and WebGPU.
Verifies add-on import paths and browser capabilities for the version; adds a fallback when rendering is unsupported.
Checks real rendering and interaction.
On teardown, cancels the animation loop, removes listeners, and disposes geometries, materials, textures, and render targets.
Measures frame time or memory when performance is part of the request.
useWhen: Building a 3D product configurator with GLTF, PBR, and env maps.
Making a game or 3D data visualization (BufferGeometry, Points).
Building a 360-degree panorama or a WebXR experience.
Adding particles, postprocessing (bloom, SSAO), or WebGPU compute shaders.
avoidWhen: You only need a procedural fragment shader: use ak-shader.
You need 3D inside a Remotion video: use ak-remotion (rule 3d.md).
A landing page with light 3D where design is the focus: use ak-frontend-design (3D workflow).
2D charts: use the dataviz skill.

params.name: [3D scene or feature]
params.desc: The 3D scene or feature to build (e.g. configurator, particles, XR).

examples.cmd: /ak:threejs product configurator for shoes with material color switching
examples.note: GLTF + PBR + color picking interaction.
Level 5 WebGPU.
Low-complexity use case.
Look up camera class APIs.

tips: Check the three version before copying a recipe; add-on APIs and TSL change between releases.
Always dispose GPU resources on unmount to avoid memory leaks.
Use instancing, LOD, and batching (12-performance.md) for scenes with many objects.
The search script needs Python 3.
artifacts: Three.js scene code (JS/TS) in the project

ak-shader.tagline: Write GLSL fragment shaders for procedural graphics: SDF, noise, fBm, patterns.
ak-shader.summary: ak:shader guides writing GPU fragment shaders for procedural textures, distance-field shapes, patterns, noise, gradients, and animated effects. Input is the desired effect or pattern; output is GLSL compatible with the target renderer (WebGL, Three.js, Processing), compiled and visually checked. References cover fundamentals, drawing, procedural techniques, and the API.
howItWorks: Inspects the real renderer, WebGL/GLSL version, precision, and uniform names and types.
Sample snippets are GLSL ES 1; GLSL ES 3 projects need the matching interface.
Loads only the references the effect needs: shaping functions, colors, SDF shapes, patterns, noise, cellular/voronoi, fBm, procedural textures, builtin API.
Uses standard uniforms (u_time, u_resolution, u_mouse) and normalized coordinates st = gl_FragCoord.xy / u_resolution.
Uses functions such as mix, step, smoothstep, and fract.
Compiles and renders in the target environment, checks the image, and measures performance per the brief; syntax validation alone is not enough.
Keeps existing uniform ownership and lifecycle intact.
useWhen: Creating procedural textures such as wood, marble, clouds, or terrain.
Drawing shapes with signed distance fields (circle, rectangle, polygon, star).
Generating Perlin/simplex/cellular noise or fBm for generative art.
Writing custom shaders for Three.js materials or WebGL backgrounds.

ak-ai-multimodal.tagline: Analyze and generate images, audio, video, and documents; native vision first, Multix fallback.
ak-ai-multimodal.summary: ak:ai-multimodal handles audio, images, video, and documents. For image/document understanding (OCR, description, extraction) it prefers the session model's native vision. It uses the @mrgoonie/multix CLI (npm latest via npx) only when native vision is ineligible, or for image/video generation, TTS, music, and transcription with a configured provider (Gemini, OpenRouter, MiniMax).
howItWorks: Routes first: image/document understanding goes to native vision; image generation/editing, video generation, and TTS/music/transcription go to Multix if a matching key exists.
Falls back to Multix for visual analysis only when the session lacks vision, input exceeds limits (long video, unsupported format, huge document), or the user asks; it states why.
Checks that GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or MINIMAX_API_KEY is present (never prints values) and routes only to a provider whose key covers the capability.
With no valid route, names the blocker (no native capability, missing credential, unsupported task, provider mismatch) and the required env var; it does not guess.
Loads references/setup.md before the first Multix run (Node, keys, multix check), then the modality reference.
Modality references: vision-understanding, image-generation, audio-processing, music-generation, video-analysis, video-generation, cli-recipes.
Before generating, runs multix ... --help on npm latest, checks the provider's model catalog and pricing, and picks an explicit model, recording it for reproducibility.
Splits oversized media with ffmpeg, processes each chunk, and merges results.
Transcripts are Markdown with metadata and [HH:MM:SS -> HH:MM:SS] lines.
useWhen: Transcribing long audio/video into a timestamped transcript.
Generating or editing images with a configured provider key.
Generating short videos, music, or TTS (MiniMax).
Analyzing long videos or documents beyond the model's native vision limits.
avoidWhen: The current model can read the image/document itself: use native vision, no Multix call needed.
You need curated prompts for marketing images: use ak-ai-artist (which still renders through this skill).
Converting or encoding media with FFmpeg/ImageMagick: use ak-media-processing.

Put keys in the shell, the project .env, or ~/.multix/.env; a key for one modality does not authorize routing another.
On provider API errors, keep the (key-redacted) error and retry only after fixing auth, billing, quota, model access, or parameters.
Never assume a 'latest/default' model; always check the current provider catalog.

Source files are kept by default; in-place edits need explicit overwrite scope.
howItWorks: Prefers the user's or repo's output paths; invokes asset organization only when arranging many assets is part of the task.
Picks the tool: FFmpeg for video encode/convert, audio extraction, thumbnails, and GIFs from video.
ImageMagick handles image resize, effects, and batch jobs (mogrify); RMBG removes backgrounds with local AI.

Loads references when needed: ffmpeg-encoding, ffmpeg-streaming, ffmpeg-filters, imagemagick-editing, imagemagick-batch, rmbg-background-removal, common-workflows, format-compatibility, troubleshooting.
Runs commands or helper scripts (media_convert.py, video_optimize.py, batch_resize.py, remove-background.sh, batch-remove-background.sh).
Writes batch output to a separate folder, keeps sources, then verifies codec, size, duration, or image metadata.

Extracting audio from video, or creating thumbnails and GIFs.

ak-hyperframes.tagline: Wrap HeyGen's HyperFrames CLI to render videos from HTML compositions.
ak-hyperframes.summary: ak:hyperframes is a docs-and-commands wrapper for HeyGen's hyperframes CLI: it vendors no HeyGen source or agent skills, and runs the npm package via npx at a pinned version (hyperframes@0.7.99, owned by references/render-workflow.md). A composition is plain HTML with data-composition-id, data-width, and data-height on the root, and data-start/data-duration/data-track-index plus class="clip" on timed elements. Output is a local MP4 (or a cloud render with HEYGEN_API_KEY), done only when ffprobe confirms it; HyperFrames is the kit's default HTML video engine, with nexu-io/html-video as a documented alternative.
howItWorks: Checks prerequisites with node scripts/verify-prereqs.mjs (--json for machine output): Node.js 22+ and FFmpeg on PATH.
It prints READY on success, otherwise platform-specific fix commands; the result is reused until the environment changes.
init: npx -y hyperframes@0.7.99 init <name> --resolution <preset> scaffolds a composition project; without --resolution the template size is kept (usually 1920x1080).
Edits the HTML composition directly per the data-* contract in references/composition-basics.md.
There is no compile step; the runtime shows and hides class="clip" elements itself.
preview: npx -y hyperframes@0.7.99 preview <name> serves a local scrubbable timeline to check data-start/data-duration order before rendering.
Only preview processes started by this task get stopped.
lint always runs before render: npx -y hyperframes@0.7.99 lint <name>.
lint fails on a missing/duplicate data-composition-id, unparseable data-start/data-duration, or timed elements without class="clip".
render: npx -y hyperframes@0.7.99 render <name> --output ./assets/videos/<name>.mp4.
Cloud rendering is a separate top-level command, hyperframes cloud render (needs HEYGEN_API_KEY); render has no --engine/cloud flag.
Verifies with ffprobe -v error -show_streams -show_format -of json <file>.mp4; done only when duration is non-zero and width/height match.
If the installed version differs from the pin, reports installed vs expected and fixes the invocation; never upgrades silently.
useWhen: Short vertical social videos (1080x1920, 9:16) built from HTML/CSS.
Product launch clips, promo loops, or motion graphics written as HTML compositions instead of React components or a timeline editor.
The composition's source of truth is HTML markup with data-composition-id/data-start timing attributes.
You need HeyGen cloud rendering (hyperframes cloud render) or self-hosted distributed rendering via lambda (AWS) or cloudrun (GCP).
avoidWhen: React component trees, frame-exact interpolation, or Remotion's audio/caption ecosystem: use ak-remotion.
Only encoding, trimming, transcoding, thumbnails, HLS/DASH, or FFmpeg/ImageMagick batches: use ak-media-processing.
Static HTML previews, slides, docs, or demos with no MP4: use ak-preview or ak-show-off.

params.desc: Composition name/path or the HyperFrames command to run (init, preview, lint, render, cloud render...).

params.desc: Scaffold a new composition project, e.g. init my-composition --resolution portrait. Run init --help to confirm current flags; the list may lag upstream.

params.desc: init flag: landscape (1920x1080), portrait (1080x1920), landscape-4k (3840x2160), portrait-4k (2160x3840), square (1080x1080), square-4k (2160x2160), plus aliases 1080p, 4k, uhd, 1080p-square, square-1080p, 4k-square.

params.desc: Serve the composition locally with a scrubbable timeline; open the printed local URL.

params.desc: Check data-* attributes and timing; must run and pass cleanly before render.

params.desc: Render an MP4 locally (Chromium capture, then FFmpeg encode) with --output <path>; no HEYGEN_API_KEY needed.

params.desc: Top-level commands for self-hosted distributed rendering on AWS (lambda) or GCP (cloudrun). (not documented in source)

tips: Requires Node.js 22+ and FFmpeg on PATH; HEYGEN_API_KEY is only for cloud render.
Store HEYGEN_API_KEY per the project's secret convention (e.g. .agentkit/.env) and never log it.
A blank or oddly short MP4 usually means a wrong data-start or data-composition-id; running lint first catches most render errors.
Do not hand-write CSS opacity/visibility for data-start; the runtime handles every class="clip" element.
Overlapping clips need different data-track-index values to set stacking order.
If the CLI reports an unknown flag, the pin may lag upstream: run the pinned command with --help before updating the pin.
For advanced techniques (keyframes, captions, product-launch templates), install HeyGen's agent skills with the skills command instead of rewriting them.
Consider nexu-io/html-video only if the user already has its binary/checkout or its template catalog fits; HyperFrames stays the default.

ak-agent-browser.tagline: Automate tool-managed browsers with agent-browser: snapshots, clicks, forms, tests.

howItWorks: Decides first: tasks that need the real Chrome profile (cookies, signed-in accounts, workspaces) go to ak:chrome-profile; everything else stays here.
If the binary or browser is missing or needs an upgrade, loads references/setup-and-upgrade.md; reuses a working binary instead of reinstalling routinely.
Before any command, loads workflow content from the CLI: agent-browser skills get core (--full for the complete command reference and templates).
For special tasks, loads a specialized skill: electron, slack, dogfood (QA/bug hunting), vercel-sandbox, agentcore; list them with agent-browser skills list.
Executes: opens the page, snapshots (-i) to get @eN refs, clicks or fills forms, takes screenshots.
Re-runs snapshot after every page change.
Cloud browser: set BROWSERBASE_API_KEY and BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID, then agent-browser -p browserbase open <url>; monitor via the dashboard on port 4848.

Exploratory QA or bug hunting with the dogfood skill.
Automating Electron apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma) or a Slack workspace.
Running browsers in CI via Browserbase or AWS AgentCore.

ak-chrome-profile.tagline: Target the user's real Chrome profile for automation via Chrome DevTools MCP.
ak-chrome-profile.summary: ak:chrome-profile provides the chrome-profile CLI, which opens a URL in the exact Chrome profile (Google account, cookies, workspace, tenant, session). It appends a #cdp-profile=<key>&cdp-open=<token> marker so the agent picks the exact tab from the Chrome DevTools MCP page list. Output is a bound tab ready for snapshot, click, evaluate, and screenshots; it is not the default for ordinary browser testing.
howItWorks: Decides first whether the task needs the real Chrome profile; if not, uses ak:agent-browser, ak:web-testing, or plain Chrome DevTools MCP navigation.
Checks 3 readiness layers: chrome-profile list resolves the key; a live Chrome DevTools MCP probe can list and read pages; after opening, the page list contains the exact cdp-open=<token>.
Missing mapping: guides through chrome-profile setup.
Suspected bridge problems: runs chrome-profile doctor, then a live MCP probe (list pages), before asking the user to change config or restart Chrome.
Opens the tab with chrome-profile open --json <key> <url> and takes bind_selector from the JSON.
Lists pages via MCP, picks the tab whose URL contains the exact cdp-open=<token>, confirms cdp-profile=<key>, then snapshots, clicks, evaluates, or screenshots.
Never uses MCP new_page or navigate_page to create profile tabs; if an SPA rewrites the hash, saves the page ID right after opening.
useWhen: Working in GitHub, Gmail, or Google Workspace with the exact signed-in account.
The user has several Chrome profiles and one must be targeted precisely.
The task needs cookies or a tenant open in everyday Chrome.
Opening a tab for the user in a specific profile (including background on macOS).
avoidWhen: A fresh, tool-managed browser is enough: use ak-agent-browser.
Repeatable CI tests: use ak-web-testing or the project's Playwright.
The browser is not Google Chrome stable: the CLI does not support it.
OS-level app window control: use computer-use.

params.desc: Profile key to target, resolved by Google account email or a display-name substring (maps to the key argument of chrome-profile open); never a folder name like 'Profile 17'.

params.desc: Select a tab by title or URL. (not documented in source; SKILL.md requires binding the tab via the cdp-open=<token> bind_selector rather than picking the newest tab)

params.desc: chrome-profile open <key> <url>: open a URL in the profile; --json prints bind data (bind_selector, opened_url, profile_key...); --force opens even without a detected readable bridge; --no-activate (macOS) returns focus to the previous app; --show-emails shows full emails.

params.desc: Discover profiles and write profiles.json ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/chrome-profile/profiles.json); --yes/-y accepts inferred keys, --non-interactive.

params.desc: Show configured keys and the profiles they resolve to on this machine.

params.desc: List every Chrome profile on the machine (no config needed).

tips: Requires Python 3.9+ and Google Chrome stable; works on macOS, Linux, and Windows.
The first MCP call may trigger Chrome's remote-control permission dialog; ask the user to approve, then retry once.
An unresolved key means the Google account is not signed into a profile on this machine; sign in once via the Chrome UI.
The CLI reads only Local State metadata, never cookies or passwords; do not reveal email/profile mappings unless needed.
For background use on macOS, add --no-activate or set CHROME_PROFILE_NO_ACTIVATE=1.
artifacts: Chrome tab opened with the #cdp-profile=<key>&cdp-open=<token> marker
